01-01.event: Giuseppe Piazzi discovered Ceres, the first asteroid found and now classed as a dwarf planet.
Edwin Hubble's measurements of Cepheid variables in the Andromeda 'nebula' were presented to the American Astronomical Society, showing it to be a separate galaxy far beyond the Milky Way.
Fabiola Gianotti, who had presented ATLAS's Higgs discovery results in 2012, took office as the first woman Director-General of CERN.

01-02.event: Paul Dirac's paper introducing his relativistic equation for the electron was received by the Royal Society. It predicted antimatter four years before the positron was found.

01-06.event: Alfred Wegener first presented his theory of continental drift, at a meeting of the Geological Association in Frankfurt.

01-07.event: Galileo Galilei first observed moons orbiting Jupiter, spotting three that night and the fourth within days, the first moons found orbiting a planet other than Earth.

01-08.event: Pyotr Kapitsa and, separately, John Allen and Don Misener published the discovery of superfluidity in liquid helium in the same issue of Nature.
Stephen Hawking was born in Oxford, England.

01-09.event: Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail published the discovery of planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12, the first confirmed planets beyond the Solar System.

01-14.event: The Huygens probe landed on Saturn's moon Titan, the most distant landing ever made on another world.

01-15.event: Sofia Kovalevskaya was born in Moscow. She made major contributions to analysis and the mechanics of rotating bodies, and became the first woman to hold a full professorship in mathematics in Northern Europe.
Irène and Frédéric Joliot-Curie announced the discovery of artificial radioactivity, created by bombarding aluminium with alpha particles.
Columbia University announced Chien-Shiung Wu's experiment showing that parity is not conserved in weak interactions, overturning a fundamental assumed symmetry of nature.
The Hubble Deep Field was released, revealing around 3,000 galaxies in a patch of sky smaller than a grain of sand held at arm's length.

01-16.event: Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 performed the first docking of two crewed spacecraft in orbit.

01-23.event: David Hilbert was born in Königsberg, Prussia.

01-25.event: Joseph-Louis Lagrange was born in Turin. His reformulation of mechanics is the starting point for modern theoretical physics.
CERN announced the discovery of the W boson, a carrier of the weak force, from events recorded by the UA1 and UA2 experiments.

01-27.event: Erwin Schrödinger's first paper on wave mechanics, introducing his wave equation, was received by Annalen der Physik.
The Outer Space Treaty, the foundational framework of international space law, was opened for signature.

01-31.event: Explorer 1, the first US satellite, was launched. Its instruments led to the discovery of the Van Allen radiation belts.

02-02.event: Patrick Blackett's paper on cloud-chamber photographs of alpha particles striking nitrogen was submitted, giving the first visual record of a nuclear transmutation (nitrogen-14 into oxygen-17), six years after Rutherford first detected the reaction.

02-03.event: Léon Foucault first publicly demonstrated his pendulum at the Paris Observatory, giving direct visual proof of Earth's rotation.
The Soviet Luna 9 probe achieved the first successful soft landing on the Moon.

02-05.event: Klaus von Klitzing discovered the quantum Hall effect, in which Hall resistance is quantised in units set only by fundamental constants.

02-09.event: The JET tokamak in England announced a record 59 megajoules of sustained fusion energy over five seconds.

02-11.event: Josiah Willard Gibbs was born in New Haven, Connecticut. He founded much of modern thermodynamics and statistical mechanics.
Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch published their explanation of nuclear fission in Nature, coining the term and calculating the enormous energy released.
The LIGO collaboration announced the first direct detection of gravitational waves, from two colliding black holes.

02-14.event: ENIAC, one of the first general-purpose electronic computers, was unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania. Its early jobs included calculations for nuclear weapons research.
Voyager 1 took the 'Pale Blue Dot' photograph of Earth from about 6 billion kilometres away.

02-15.event: Galileo Galilei was born in Pisa, Italy.
The Chelyabinsk meteor exploded over Russia, the largest airburst since the 1908 Tunguska event.

02-18.event: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto at Lowell Observatory.

02-19.event: Nicolaus Copernicus was born in Toruń, Poland.

02-20.event: Ludwig Boltzmann was born in Vienna. His statistical interpretation of entropy founded statistical mechanics.
John Glenn became the first American to orbit the Earth, aboard Friendship 7.

02-22.event: NASA announced seven Earth-sized planets orbiting the nearby star TRAPPIST-1, three of them in the habitable zone.

02-24.event: Supernova 1987A was discovered in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the closest observed supernova since 1604. Its neutrinos, detected hours before the light, opened the field of neutrino astronomy.

02-27.event: James Chadwick published his discovery of the neutron, explaining the penetrating radiation from beryllium first seen by Bothe and Becker and studied by Irène and Frédéric Joliot-Curie.

02-28.event: C. V. Raman discovered the inelastic scattering of light now called the Raman effect. India celebrates the date as National Science Day.

03-02.event: Henri Becquerel reported that uranium salts emit penetrating rays without any light exposure, the discovery of radioactivity.
Fermilab's CDF and D0 experiments jointly announced the discovery of the top quark, the heaviest known elementary particle and the last quark to be found.

03-03.event: Henrietta Leavitt's period-luminosity relation for Cepheid variables was published, giving astronomers their first standard candle for measuring distances to other galaxies.

03-06.event: Joseph von Fraunhofer was born in Straubing, Bavaria. He mapped the dark absorption lines in the Sun's spectrum that founded astronomical spectroscopy.
NASA launched the Kepler space telescope to search for exoplanets.

03-12.event: Tim Berners-Lee submitted his proposal for an information management system at CERN, the origin of the World Wide Web.

03-13.event: William Herschel discovered Uranus, the first planet found with a telescope.

03-14.event: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, Germany.
Stephen Hawking died in Cambridge, on the anniversary of Einstein's birth.

03-16.event: Caroline Herschel was born in Hanover. She went on to discover eight comets and became the first woman paid as a scientist in Britain.
Maarten Schmidt published the redshift of 3C 273, revealing quasars as extremely luminous objects billions of light-years away.

03-18.event: Albert Einstein's paper explaining the photoelectric effect with light quanta was received by Annalen der Physik, the work later cited for his Nobel Prize.

03-21.event: Joseph Fourier was born in Auxerre, France. His series and transforms, developed to study heat flow, are used across all of physics.
The Planck satellite released its first full-sky map of the cosmic microwave background, refining the age of the universe to about 13.8 billion years.

03-23.event: Emmy Noether was born in Erlangen, Germany. Her theorem linking symmetries to conservation laws underpins modern physics.
Werner Heisenberg's paper introducing the uncertainty principle was received by Zeitschrift für Physik.

03-25.event: Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan, Saturn's largest moon.

03-30.event: The Large Hadron Collider recorded its first proton collisions at 7 TeV, a world record energy at the time.

04-08.event: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes's lab observed the electrical resistance of mercury vanish below about 4 kelvin, the discovery of superconductivity.

04-10.event: The Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of a black hole's shadow, at the centre of galaxy M87.

04-12.event: Yuri Gagarin became the first human to travel into space, aboard Vostok 1.

04-14.event: Christiaan Huygens was born in The Hague. His wave theory of light explained reflection and refraction.
John Cockcroft and Ernest Walton split lithium nuclei with artificially accelerated protons at the Cavendish Laboratory, the first fully artificial nuclear reaction.

04-15.event: Leonhard Euler was born in Basel, Switzerland.

04-18.event: NASA launched TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, to search the nearest and brightest stars for planets.

04-21.event: Hans Christian Ørsted noticed an electric current deflecting a compass needle during a lecture, the first evidence linking electricity and magnetism.

04-23.event: Max Planck was born in Kiel, Germany.
The COBE team announced the detection of tiny temperature fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background, the seeds of all later cosmic structure.

04-24.event: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery.

04-25.event: Wolfgang Pauli was born in Vienna. His exclusion principle explains the structure of the periodic table.
Watson and Crick's paper proposing the double-helix structure of DNA was published in Nature, alongside papers by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins whose X-ray data underpinned it.

04-26.event: Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis held the 'Great Debate' over the size of the Milky Way and whether spiral nebulae are separate galaxies.
Reactor 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant exploded, the worst nuclear power accident in history.

04-29.event: Henri Poincaré was born in Nancy, France. His work on the three-body problem laid the foundations of chaos theory.

04-30.event: Carl Friedrich Gauss was born in Brunswick, Germany.
J. J. Thomson announced at the Royal Institution that cathode rays are made of particles far smaller than atoms, the discovery of the electron.
CERN released the World Wide Web software into the public domain, allowing anyone to use and build on it for free.

05-10.event: Augustin-Jean Fresnel was born in Broglie, France. His work on diffraction established the wave theory of light.
Cecilia Payne-Gaposchkin was born in Wendover, England. Her 1925 thesis showed that stars are made overwhelmingly of hydrogen and helium.

05-11.event: Albert Einstein's paper on Brownian motion was received by Annalen der Physik, giving decisive evidence for the existence of atoms.
Richard Feynman was born in New York City.

05-12.event: The Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of Sagittarius A*, the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.

05-13.event: Inge Lehmann was born in Copenhagen. She discovered from seismic waves that Earth has a solid inner core.

05-14.event: The United States launched Skylab, its first space station.

05-15.event: Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen published their paper questioning whether quantum mechanics is complete, the origin of the debate over entanglement.

05-16.event: Theodore Maiman operated the first working laser, using a ruby crystal, at Hughes Research Laboratories.
Joseph Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin published the discovery of the Antarctic ozone hole in Nature.

05-17.event: James Clerk Maxwell demonstrated the first colour photograph, of a tartan ribbon, at the Royal Institution, using his three-colour method.

05-20.event: The redefined SI took effect, with the kilogram, ampere, kelvin and mole defined by fixed values of fundamental constants instead of physical artefacts.

05-25.event: Christian Doppler presented his paper on how the observed frequency of a wave depends on the motion of its source, the Doppler effect.
President Kennedy announced the goal of landing a man on the Moon before the end of the decade.

05-29.event: Arthur Eddington's solar eclipse expedition measured starlight bending around the Sun, providing early observational support for general relativity.
Peter Higgs was born in Newcastle upon Tyne, England.

05-30.event: Hannes Alfvén was born in Norrköping, Sweden. He founded magnetohydrodynamics and much of modern plasma physics.

05-31.event: Chien-Shiung Wu was born in Liuhe, China. She became one of the foremost experimental physicists of the 20th century.

06-01.event: Sadi Carnot was born in Paris. His analysis of heat engines founded thermodynamics.
CERN announced the discovery of the Z boson, the neutral carrier of the weak force, completing the electroweak picture.

06-04.event: Satyendra Nath Bose wrote to Einstein enclosing his derivation of Planck's law, the foundation of Bose-Einstein statistics.

06-05.event: Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman created the first Bose-Einstein condensate, in rubidium atoms cooled to 170 nanokelvin at JILA.

06-10.event: Bernhard Riemann gave his habilitation lecture on the foundations of geometry, introducing the curved-space mathematics Einstein later used for general relativity.

06-13.event: Thomas Young was born in Milverton, England. His double-slit experiment demonstrated the wave nature of light.
James Clerk Maxwell was born in Edinburgh, Scotland.

06-14.event: Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines telegrammed Wolfgang Pauli that they had detected the neutrino, 26 years after he proposed it.

06-16.event: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space, aboard Vostok 6.

06-18.event: Sally Ride became the first American woman in space, aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger. She held a PhD in physics from Stanford.

06-22.event: Galileo Galilei was convicted by the Roman Inquisition for advocating heliocentrism and forced to recant.

06-23.event: Alan Turing was born in London.
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory released its first images, beginning a decade-long survey of the southern sky.

06-25.event: The Joint European Torus (JET) produced its first plasma, beginning 40 years as the world's largest operating tokamak.

06-26.event: William Thomson, later Lord Kelvin, was born in Belfast. He established the absolute temperature scale that bears his name.
Lyman Spitzer was born in Toledo, Ohio. He invented the stellarator for fusion research and first proposed a space telescope.

06-27.event: The Obninsk Nuclear Power Plant in the Soviet Union became the first nuclear reactor to supply electricity to a power grid.

06-28.event: Maria Goeppert Mayer was born in Kattowitz, Germany. Her nuclear shell model made her the second woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.

06-30.event: Albert Einstein's paper on special relativity, 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', was received by Annalen der Physik.
The Tunguska event flattened about 2,000 square kilometres of Siberian forest, the largest impact event in recorded history.

07-01.event: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons was opened for signature.
The ATLAS survey discovered 3I/ATLAS, only the third known interstellar object to pass through the Solar System.

07-02.event: The US Vela satellites, built to detect nuclear tests, recorded the first gamma-ray burst. The discovery stayed classified until 1973.

07-03.event: Raymond Damadian's team made the first MRI scan of a human body, taking nearly five hours to produce a single image.

07-04.event: Chinese astronomers recorded a 'guest star' bright enough to see in daylight, the supernova that created the Crab Nebula.
Henrietta Leavitt was born in Lancaster, Massachusetts.
Marie Curie died in France, the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
CERN announced the discovery of a particle consistent with the Higgs boson, using data from the ATLAS and CMS experiments, nearly 50 years after it was predicted.

07-05.event: Isaac Newton's Principia Mathematica was published, setting out his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

07-07.event: The first Pugwash Conference on Science and World Affairs convened in Nova Scotia, bringing scientists from both sides of the Cold War together on nuclear risk.

07-09.event: The Russell-Einstein Manifesto was issued in London, warning of the dangers of nuclear weapons. Einstein signed it days before his death.

07-10.event: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes liquefied helium for the first time, reaching about 4 kelvin.

07-12.event: The James Webb Space Telescope released its first full-colour science images.

07-14.event: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft performed its closest flyby of Pluto, returning the first detailed images of the dwarf planet.
CERN's LHCb experiment announced the discovery of pentaquarks, exotic particles made of five quarks.

07-15.event: Jocelyn Bell Burnell was born in Lurgan, Northern Ireland.
Mariner 4 made the first successful flyby of Mars, returning the first close-up images of another planet.

07-16.event: The Trinity test in New Mexico became the first detonation of a nuclear weapon.
The first fragment of comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 struck Jupiter, the first collision of two Solar System bodies ever observed.

07-18.event: Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of polonium, named after Marie's native Poland.

07-19.event: CERN's Gargamelle bubble chamber collaboration presented the first evidence of weak neutral currents, a key prediction of electroweak theory.

07-20.event: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon.
Viking 1 became the first spacecraft to land successfully on Mars and carry out its mission.

07-21.event: Fermilab's DONUT experiment announced the first direct observation of the tau neutrino, the last Standard Model lepton to be detected.

07-23.event: Felix Klein presented Emmy Noether's paper containing her theorem, linking every continuous symmetry to a conservation law, to the Göttingen Mathematical Society.
Vera Rubin was born in Philadelphia. Her galaxy rotation curves became key evidence for dark matter.
NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory was launched aboard the Space Shuttle Columbia.

07-25.event: Rosalind Franklin was born in London. Her X-ray diffraction images were key to determining the structure of DNA.

07-29.event: Werner Heisenberg's paper laying the foundations of matrix mechanics, written after a stay on the island of Helgoland, was received by Zeitschrift für Physik.

08-01.event: Caroline Herschel discovered her first comet, becoming the first woman credited with discovering one.

08-02.event: Carl Anderson took the cloud-chamber photograph of a positively charged electron, the positron, the first antimatter particle observed.
Albert Einstein signed a letter drafted with Leo Szilard warning President Roosevelt that Germany might develop atomic bombs, prompting US nuclear research.

08-05.event: The Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty was signed in Moscow, banning nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in space and underwater.
Fermilab publicly announced the Upsilon particle, discovered by Leon Lederman's E288 team, the first evidence of the bottom quark.

08-06.event: An atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima, Japan, the first use of a nuclear weapon in war.
NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars.

08-08.event: David Hilbert presented his famous list of unsolved problems at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Paris. His sixth problem called for an axiomatisation of physics.
Paul Dirac was born in Bristol, England.
Roger Penrose was born in Colchester, England.

08-12.event: Erwin Schrödinger was born in Vienna.
NASA launched the Parker Solar Probe to fly through the Sun's outer atmosphere.

08-17.event: LIGO and Virgo detected gravitational waves from two merging neutron stars, also seen across the electromagnetic spectrum, the birth of multi-messenger astronomy.

08-18.event: During a solar eclipse, Jules Janssen observed an unknown yellow spectral line from the Sun, later identified as a new element, helium.

08-20.event: Voyager 2 was launched, beginning a tour of all four giant planets.

08-24.event: The International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.
Astronomers announced Proxima b, a planet orbiting in the habitable zone of the nearest star to the Sun.

08-25.event: Voyager 2 made its closest approach to Neptune, the only spacecraft to have visited the planet.
Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, becoming the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

08-26.event: Katherine Johnson was born in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia. Her orbital calculations were essential to early NASA crewed flights.
Edward Witten was born in Baltimore. He is the only physicist to have won the Fields Medal.

08-29.event: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, the principle behind every electric generator and transformer.

08-30.event: Ernest Rutherford was born in Brightwater, New Zealand.

09-01.event: Richard Carrington observed a solar flare that triggered the most intense geomagnetic storm on record, the Carrington Event.

09-05.event: Voyager 1 was launched. It is now the most distant human-made object.

09-06.event: Jocelyn Bell Burnell won the Breakthrough Prize for her discovery of pulsars, and donated the $3 million to fund physics PhDs for under-represented students.

09-10.event: The first proton beam circulated around the Large Hadron Collider at CERN.

09-14.event: LIGO detected gravitational waves for the first time, from two black holes merging 1.3 billion light-years away. The detection was announced the following February.

09-15.event: The Cassini spacecraft ended its 13-year mission at Saturn with a deliberate plunge into the planet's atmosphere.

09-16.event: The Montreal Protocol was signed to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals. It became the first treaty ratified by every country in the world.

09-22.event: Michael Faraday was born in Newington Butts, London.
IceCube detected a high-energy neutrino later traced to the blazar TXS 0506+056, the first identified source of high-energy cosmic neutrinos.

09-23.event: Johann Galle observed Neptune for the first time, within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier had predicted it from irregularities in Uranus's orbit.

09-26.event: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judged a satellite warning of incoming nuclear missiles to be a false alarm, a decision credited with averting potential nuclear war.

09-27.event: Albert Einstein's paper showing that a body's mass depends on its energy content, the origin of E = mc², was received by Annalen der Physik.

09-29.event: Enrico Fermi was born in Rome, Italy.
CERN was officially founded, as its convention came into force.

10-01.event: The first CT scan of a patient was performed at Atkinson Morley Hospital in London, using Godfrey Hounsfield's scanner.

10-02.event: Donna Strickland shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for chirped pulse amplification of laser light, the third woman ever to win it.

10-03.event: Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish and Kip Thorne were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the detection of gravitational waves by LIGO.
Anne L'Huillier, Pierre Agostini and Ferenc Krausz were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for attosecond pulses of light, making L'Huillier the fifth woman to win it.

10-04.event: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth.
Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the accelerating expansion of the universe.
Alain Aspect, John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments with entangled photons.

10-05.event: Syukuro Manabe, Klaus Hasselmann and Giorgio Parisi were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for climate modelling and for the physics of complex disordered systems.

10-06.event: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced 51 Pegasi b, the first exoplanet found orbiting a Sun-like star.
Charles Kao, Willard Boyle and George Smith were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for optical fibre communication and the CCD image sensor.
Takaaki Kajita and Arthur McDonald were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering neutrino oscillations, showing neutrinos have mass.
Andrea Ghez shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, the fourth woman to win it.

10-07.event: Niels Bohr was born in Copenhagen, Denmark.

10-08.event: François Englert and Peter Higgs were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for the mechanism that gives elementary particles mass.

10-09.event: A new star was first sighted in Ophiuchus. Johannes Kepler's detailed study of it made it known as Kepler's Supernova, the last supernova seen in the Milky Way.
Serge Haroche and David Wineland were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for methods to measure and control individual quantum systems, including trapped ions.

10-16.event: William Rowan Hamilton discovered quaternions while walking along a canal in Dublin, and carved the formula into Brougham Bridge.

10-17.event: Calder Hall in England opened as the world's first commercial-scale nuclear power station.

10-19.event: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was born in Lahore. His mass limit for white dwarfs underpins the theory of stellar death.
The Pan-STARRS telescope discovered 'Oumuamua, the first known interstellar object to pass through the Solar System.

10-22.event: Enrico Fermi's group in Rome discovered that slowing neutrons with paraffin wax greatly increases their ability to induce radioactivity, a key step towards nuclear reactors.
Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov published the isolation of graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms, using sticky tape.

10-23.event: Google published its claim of quantum supremacy, with the Sycamore processor completing in minutes a task estimated to take a classical supercomputer thousands of years.

10-24.event: The fifth Solvay Conference opened in Brussels, where Einstein and Bohr began their famous debates over quantum mechanics.

11-01.event: The United States detonated Ivy Mike at Enewetak Atoll, the first full-scale thermonuclear device, roughly 700 times more powerful than the Hiroshima bomb.

11-07.event: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw, Poland.
Lise Meitner was born in Vienna, sharing a birthday with Marie Curie.
C. V. Raman was born in Tiruchirappalli, India, completing a remarkable trio of physicists born on this date.

11-09.event: Albert Einstein was awarded the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, for his explanation of the photoelectric effect rather than relativity.
Carl Sagan was born in Brooklyn, New York.

11-11.event: Tycho Brahe observed a brilliant new star in Cassiopeia, a supernova whose fixed position helped overturn the idea of an unchanging heavens.
Mildred Dresselhaus was born in Brooklyn. Her work on carbon nanostructures earned her the nickname 'Queen of Carbon Science'.
SLAC and Brookhaven simultaneously announced the J/psi particle, evidence for the charm quark, an event known as the November Revolution.

11-12.event: The Philae lander touched down on comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, the first landing on a comet.

11-16.event: The General Conference on Weights and Measures voted to redefine the kilogram in terms of the Planck constant, retiring the platinum-iridium cylinder kept in Paris since 1889.

11-18.event: NASA launched COBE, the Cosmic Background Explorer.

11-20.event: Edwin Hubble was born in Marshfield, Missouri.
David Hilbert submitted his own derivation of the field equations of general relativity, five days before Einstein presented his final version.

11-21.event: Seven partners, including the EU, US, China and Russia, signed the agreement to build ITER, the international fusion experiment in southern France.

11-25.event: Albert Einstein presented the final field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

11-28.event: Jocelyn Bell Burnell recorded the regular pulses of the first known pulsar, at the Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory in Cambridge.

12-02.event: The first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction was achieved at Chicago Pile-1, part of the Manhattan Project.
The Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) was launched, and became one of the longest-running solar missions.

12-05.event: Werner Heisenberg was born in Würzburg, Germany.
The National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition for the first time, producing more energy from a fusion reaction than the laser energy delivered to the target.

12-08.event: James Clerk Maxwell read 'A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field' to the Royal Society, unifying electricity, magnetism and light.

12-10.event: Wilhelm Röntgen received the first ever Nobel Prize in Physics, for his discovery of X-rays.
Marie Curie, Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for their work on radioactivity, making Marie Curie the first woman Nobel laureate.
Marie Curie was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovering polonium and radium, becoming the first person to win two Nobel Prizes.
The Wendelstein 7-X stellarator in Germany produced its first plasma.

12-11.event: Annie Jump Cannon was born in Dover, Delaware. Her stellar classification scheme, O B A F G K M, is still used today.

12-14.event: Max Planck presented his quantum hypothesis to the German Physical Society, often marking the birth of quantum theory.

12-17.event: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, the chemical evidence for nuclear fission.

12-19.event: Albert Michelson was born in Strzelno, Prussia. He became the first American to win a Nobel Prize in the sciences, for his precision optical measurements.

12-20.event: Experimental Breeder Reactor I in Idaho generated the first electricity from nuclear power, lighting four light bulbs.

12-23.event: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain demonstrated the first working transistor at Bell Labs.

12-24.event: Apollo 8 astronaut Bill Anders took the 'Earthrise' photograph while orbiting the Moon.
The Parker Solar Probe made its closest approach to the Sun, passing within about 6 million kilometres of its surface.

12-25.event: Isaac Newton was born in Woolsthorpe, England (Christmas Day by the Julian calendar then used in England).
Johann Palitzsch spotted the return of Halley's comet, confirming Edmond Halley's prediction made decades earlier.
The James Webb Space Telescope was launched from French Guiana.

12-26.event: Mary Somerville was born in Jedburgh, Scotland. Her writing on physical science led her to be described as the first 'scientist', a word coined in a review of her work.
Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of radium.

12-27.event: Johannes Kepler was born in Weil der Stadt, in what is now Germany.

12-28.event: Wilhelm Röntgen submitted his paper announcing the discovery of X-rays.
John von Neumann was born in Budapest. He gave quantum mechanics its rigorous mathematical framework.

12-29.event: Edward Lorenz gave his talk asking whether the flap of a butterfly's wings in Brazil could set off a tornado in Texas, popularising chaos theory's 'butterfly effect'.
